name: minutesPerTick
description: Simulated minutes represented by one schedule tick
mechanism: Sets the integration step for movement and exposure; 60 ticks aggregate to one hourly PM2.5 slice with no partial-hour remainder
source: Modelling decision: 1 min keeps the per-tick step (~78 m) below typical street-segment length, avoiding path overshoot
uncertainty: none

name: walkingSpeedMps
description: Resident walking speed
mechanism: Comfortable self-selected gait speed sets time outdoors, the proximate driver of accrued exposure
source: Bohannon 1997 comfortable gait speed of adults 20-79 (n=230); 1.30 is below 10 of 12 age-sex cells and ~6% under the table mean of 1.381
uncertainty: 1.272-1.462 m/s across published age-sex cells

name: evacuationThresholdUgM3
description: PM2.5 concentration at which a resident begins evacuating
mechanism: Ties evacuation to the smoke event rather than assuming everyone leaves at t0; residents shelter in place accruing exposure until the air crosses a hazard threshold
source: EPA Unhealthy AQI breakpoint lower bound, stable across the pre- and post-2024 breakpoint tables
uncertainty: convention choice; alternatives are the 24-h-average AQI category or NowCast

name: numAgents
description: Number of resident agents instantiated
mechanism: Population scale; determines whether shelter capacity binds and therefore whether refusal outcomes can occur at all. Once capacity binds, refused residents remain outdoors and keep accruing exposure, so population size feeds back into exposure
source: Demonstration value 50; production runs use the measured 2037 (class M) per decision D-5
uncertainty: 50 (regression fixture) vs 2037 (measured PIT count)

name: randomSeed
description: Master random seed
mechanism: Reproducibility infrastructure. Not inert: the seed selects each resident's encampment of origin and drives Repast's per-tick agent shuffle, so it determines routes, travel distance, accrued exposure and - once capacity binds - who is admitted
source: Infrastructure; run-to-run reproducibility verified bit-for-bit at seed 42
uncertainty: none

name: simulationHours
description: Length of the simulated event window
mechanism: Bounds the run to the September 2020 smoke episode so exposure accrues only over the studied event
source: Sept 7-19 2020 event window; capped by the available hourly PM2.5 record
uncertainty: none

name: shelterArrivalDistanceM
description: Declared arrival radius around a shelter
mechanism: Intended to represent final approach not being explicitly simulated; superseded once routing terminated agents exactly at shelter-adjacent street nodes
source: Declared in parameters.xml and recorded in the manifest but consumed by no code path
uncertainty: none

name: smokeField
description: County-uniform hourly PM2.5 concentration field
mechanism: The only environmental driver; regional smoke inundation raised concentrations roughly 100x above baseline for about nine days
math: C(t) = hourly mean of in-county monitors
source: EPA AQS hourly PM2.5 parameter 88502, Multnomah County monitors; peak 562.7 ug/m3
uncertainty: spatially uniform; an IDW alternative is specified but unjustified with 2 in-county monitors

name: cumulative_dose_ugm3h
description: Cumulative outdoor PM2.5 exposure per resident
mechanism: Time-integrated concentration breathed while outdoors; accrual stops at shelter arrival because arrival is the study endpoint
math: sum over ticks of C(t) * dt
source: Derived from the measured concentration field and simulated time outdoors
uncertainty: none

name: vwe_ugm3h
description: Exposure Burden Index (EBI); historically named VWE
mechanism: Susceptibility-weighted exposure index; the machine column name is retained for backward compatibility per decision D-2
math: sum of C(t) * RR_age * RR_com * dt
source: An index with assumed weights, not an epidemiological prediction; identical to raw exposure while weights are 1.0
uncertainty: weights swept 1.0-2.5 as a labelled sensitivity, never as a headline

name: age_rr
description: Age susceptibility weight
mechanism: Intended to represent age modification of the PM2.5 exposure-response; the slide-cited 1.45 is unsupported and the correct estimand disagrees across studies
source: UNSOURCED - Di et al 2017 cannot yield an age contrast (cohort entirely 65+); Kondo 2019 meta-RRR is 1.008 (0.996-1.020), i.e. null
uncertainty: 1.0 base; 1.0-2.5 only as an equivalent-dose sensitivity

name: comorbidity_rr
description: Comorbidity susceptibility weight
mechanism: Intended to represent asthma/COPD modification of the exposure-response; the slide-cited 1.80 traces to no existing paper
source: UNSOURCED - 'Anderson et al 2013' does not exist; pooled COPD OR equals the all-respiratory OR in the wildfire literature
uncertainty: 1.0 base; 1.0-1.6 only as an equivalent-dose sensitivity

name: hours_above_unhealthy
description: Person-hours breathing above the Unhealthy concentration breakpoint
mechanism: Burden expressed as time above a health-relevant concentration rather than as an integral
source: Counts hourly values above the EPA Unhealthy breakpoint concentration; deliberately NOT the 24-h-average AQI category
uncertainty: convention choice; a 24-h-average variant is specified as a secondary metric

name: total_travel_distance_m
description: Cumulative geodesic distance walked
mechanism: Cost of access and the distance over which outdoor exposure accrues
source: Derived; geodesic arc length on the WGS84 ellipsoid (Karney 2013)
uncertainty: none

name: network_dist_to_shelter_m
description: Shortest-path street distance to the selected shelter
mechanism: Accessibility measure - the nearest shelter a resident can actually reach on the street network
math: Dijkstra shortest path over geodesic edge weights
source: Derived from the validated street graph; algorithm Dijkstra 1959
uncertainty: none

name: shelterCapacity
description: Nightly capacity of each operating shelter
mechanism: Determines whether the allocation problem binds; refusal and equity outcomes are only possible once capacity is scarce
source: 99 per site is newsroom-sourced and unconfirmed by a primary agency document
uncertainty: unconfirmed; confirm against a primary source before quoting refusal results

name: gini
description: Gini coefficient of exposure across residents
mechanism: Equity measure distinguishing shared exposure from exposure borne by a minority
source: Derived statistic over per-agent exposure (V6) and therefore inheriting the provenance of the measured concentration field; reported for both raw exposure and the weighted index so equity claims stay separable from the weighting assumption
uncertainty: none

name: NODE_SITE_TOLERANCE_M
description: Clustering radius for street-graph node claims
mechanism: Separates legitimate sub-metre endpoint scatter from corrupt attribute IDs claimed kilometres apart, preventing wormhole edges
math: claims within tolerance form one node site
source: Numerical guard: legitimate scatter is sub-metre and the smallest corrupt displacement observed is ~1.65 km, so 100 m separates the regimes with wide margin
uncertainty: 100 m; behaviour is insensitive between roughly 1 m and 1 km given the observed gap

name: REATTACH_TOLERANCE_M
description: Radius for aliasing a corrected node site to an existing junction
mechanism: Endpoints coincident at this scale are the same physical junction so the corrected site is reattached rather than split
source: Numerical guard chosen an order of magnitude below the node-site tolerance
uncertainty: 10 m; 4 of 27 corrections were reattachments at this threshold

name: startingEncampment
description: Resident start location
mechanism: Spatial origin of each journey; sets network distance to shelter and therefore exposure
math: uniform sample over campsite report points
source: Real City of Portland IRP campsite reports, used as a spatial proxy because only 2025-26 records exist
uncertainty: temporal proxy - 2025-26 locations stand in for 2020; complaint-driven reporting implies visibility bias

name: ageYears / ageBand
description: Resident age, sampled uniformly within the published PIT age bands (adults only)
mechanism: Selects the Bohannon age-by-sex comfortable gait speed cell and defines the 55+ reporting stratum; age has NO direct exposure weight in this model
source: 2019 Multnomah County Point-in-Time count, unsheltered population N=2037, Table on age bands
uncertainty: Band shares measured; WITHIN-band shape unconstrained so age is sampled uniformly (Option A). 25-54 spans 72.7% of adults and is not subdivided

name: sex
description: Resident sex/gender category as recorded by the PIT
mechanism: Selects the sex column of the Bohannon gait-speed table and nothing else; deliberately NOT a vulnerability weight
source: 2019 Multnomah County PIT unsheltered; corroborated by HUD 2023 AHAR national unsheltered (68.2/30.1/0.9)
uncertainty: Source states stigma likely undercounts transgender and gender-non-conforming identities; residents outside male/female take the mean of the two published speed columns

name: mobilityLimited / mobilityCategory
description: Whether the resident has a mobility limitation, and which movement-speed category applies
mechanism: Replaces the age-by-sex gait speed with Boyce ambulant-impaired N(0.95,0.32) m/s by REPLACEMENT not multiplication; slower walking lengthens outdoor time and lowers the chance of reaching a bed before capacity fills
math: P(limited) = 0.1522 under 55, 0.3478 at 55+, holding the measured 0.192 marginal
source: 2019 Multnomah County PIT (391/2037 = 19.2%, LOWER BOUND: asked only of survey completers but divided by the full population); age gradient ratio from CASPEH 2023 (22% overall vs 32% at 50+)
uncertainty: 0.192 is a lower bound; convergent external evidence 0.19-0.27 (CASPEH 22%, Brown 2017 26.9%, Lewer 2019 21.0%). Aid-type mix unresolved: all limited residents get the FASTEST impaired category, so the penalty is understated
implementation: PopulationSampler.sample; GisAgent walking speed; agents.csv mobility_limited/mobility_category

name: asthma
description: Whether the resident lives with diagnosed asthma
mechanism: Reporting stratum ONLY. Asthma has no movement effect because no quantitative comfortable-gait-speed decrement was found for adults with asthma; the literature supports lower physical ACTIVITY volume, which cannot be converted to m/s without invention. Never multiplied into a dose - decision D-3
source: Zellmer et al. 2025 J Gen Intern Med, EHR-diagnosed asthma among adults with recent homelessness (n=20139): 14.9% vs 7.1% housed. NOT ACS/BRFSS/NHIS, whose housing-unit sampling frames structurally exclude unsheltered people
uncertainty: 0.15-0.24: EHR-diagnosed undercounts the never-diagnosed, self-report (Lewer 18.3%) overcounts; the two biases bracket the truth. No local Multnomah value exists at all

name: copd
description: Whether the resident lives with diagnosed COPD
mechanism: Reporting stratum AND a movement effect: COPD reduces comfortable walking speed by a verified amount (see V24), which lengthens time outdoors and lowers the chance of reaching a bed before capacity fills. COPD is never multiplied into a dose - decision D-3
source: Zellmer et al. 2025, EHR-diagnosed COPD among adults with recent homelessness: 10.5% vs 3.0% housed. Age-independence is evidence-based: Brown 2017 reports asthma-or-COPD 26.3% at 50+, essentially equal to CASPEH 25% across all ages
uncertainty: 0.04-0.14. Rappold 2011 RR 1.73 is a county-level dichotomous ED-visit estimate and must NOT be used as a person-level multiplier; the discredited 1.80 figure is never used

name: chronic_physical
description: Whether the resident lives with a long-term physical health condition
mechanism: Reporting stratum ONLY - no movement effect and never a dose multiplier. It exists so outcomes can be reported for residents with a chronic physical condition alongside the mobility, asthma and COPD strata (decision D-3: diagnosis is never a dose weight)
source: Pathways Study 2026 (PSU HRAC / OHSU), N = 541, Multnomah County: 39.1% of respondents report a long-term physical health condition. Local and contemporaneous with the 2026 shelter network
uncertainty: Single local survey, N = 541; no second local estimate exists to bracket it. Sampled independently of age for the same reason as V21a/V21b - Brown 2017 finds no material age gradient in chronic-condition prevalence in this population
implementation: PopulationSampler.sample; agents.csv chronic_physical; ContextCreator population census

name: shelterOpenTick
description: Tick from which each shelter admits residents, from its real opening date
mechanism: Residents cannot depart before somewhere is open and cannot be admitted before that date; a resident refused while only one site is open may try the second when it opens the next day
source: Real September 2020 opening dates: Oregon Convention Center 2020-09-10, Charles Jordan Community Center 2020-09-11, both through 2020-09-19
uncertainty: The source gives dates, not hours; opening is modelled at 00:00 local, the earliest defensible reading, which UNDERSTATES pre-opening outdoor exposure

name: copdSpeedDeltaMps
description: Reduction in comfortable walking speed for residents with COPD
mechanism: Applied additively to the age-by-sex comfortable gait speed before dispersion is sampled; NOT stacked on the Boyce mobility-limited speed because those categories already embed an impaired walker
source: Buekers J et al. 2024, European Respiratory Review 33(172):230253 - systematic review and meta-analysis, 25 studies, 1015 people with COPD vs 2229 healthy controls; usual-speed mean difference -19 cm/s (95% CI -28 to -11). Fast-pace difference deliberately not used. Authors rate the evidence LOW quality
uncertainty: -0.11 to -0.28 m/s (the published 95% CI); evidence rated low quality by the review authors, so the point estimate must be swept not assumed

name: inhaled_dose_ug
description: Inhaled PM2.5 mass, activity-weighted
mechanism: Exposure weighted by ventilation rate, which depends on ACTIVITY only (walking vs waiting outdoors). No health attribute enters this term - susceptibility is a separate multiplier held at 1.0. This is the physics of the person, distinct from exposure (physics of the air) and from health risk (biology)
math: sum over ticks of C(t) * IR(activity) * dt; IR = 1.62 m3/h walking, 0.61 m3/h otherwise
source: U.S. EPA Exposure Factors Handbook 2011 Chapter 6, activity-level inhalation rates for adults. VERIFIED-IN-SECONDARY: the table cells were not re-read from the primary during implementation
uncertainty: walking 1.2-2.0 m3/h, resting 0.4-0.8 m3/h; confirm against the primary before publication. Comfortable walking sits at the light/moderate boundary and the moderate cell was chosen, which is conservative in the direction that increases modelled walking dose

name: freewayTypeExclusion
description: RLIS TYPE codes excluded from the pedestrian routing graph (freeway mainlines and ramps)
mechanism: Pedestrians are prohibited on limited-access freeways, so freeway centrelines must not supply walking shortcuts or river crossings; unfiltered, 2,636 freeway-class features (~590 km) were walkable, including the Marquam (I-5) and Fremont (I-405) bridges, which carry no pedestrian access
math: exclude street feature from graph and display if TYPE in {1110, 1120, 1121, 1122, 1123}
source: Metro RLIS Streets centreline metadata: TYPE 1110 = freeway mainline, 1120-1123 = freeway ramps/connectors (same features carry CFCC A15/A63 and names of the form I5 FWY NB; verified against Streets.dbf: 1110 n=1372, 1120 n=279, 1121 n=466, 1122 n=447, 1123 n=72). Pedestrian-legal Willamette crossings are Broadway, Steel lower deck, Burnside, Morrison, Hawthorne, Tilikum, Sellwood, St Johns (round-4 delta U-27); Marquam and Fremont are not among them
uncertainty: Only unambiguous freeway classes are removed; TYPE 1200-series highways (2,139 features) are retained pending a per-segment sidewalk source - a registered sensitivity, not an oversight

name: walkingSpeedBounds
description: Truncation bounds on the sampled walking-speed distribution
mechanism: Rejection sampling re-draws until the sampled speed lies in [SPEED_MIN_MPS, SPEED_MAX_MPS]; after 100 failed draws the value clamps to the violated bound. Prevents physically meaningless speeds without reshaping the empirical distributions
math: accept v ~ TruncNormal(mu[age,sex], CV 0.13) iff 0.40 <= v <= 2.20
source: Modelling decision, published verbatim (TECHNICAL_REFERENCE.md truncatedNormal spec). 0.40 m/s floor sits below the Boyce impaired-walker mean minus 1.7 SD; 2.20 m/s cap is above every Bohannon age-sex cell mean plus 4 SD. Round-4 U-04 verified numerically: 0 of 61,578 sampled speeds hit either bound
uncertainty: Bounds are inert in practice (zero realized clamps across 9 production seeds); swept only if a future distribution change makes them bind

name: ageCeiling
description: Maximum sampled age (exclusive upper bound of the oldest decade row)
mechanism: Ages sample uniformly within PIT/Pathways bands; the open-ended 65+ band closes at 90 so the Bohannon decade lookup always lands on a published row. Ages 80-89 use the real published 80+ decade (0.968 M / 0.943 F) via the row clamp
math: age ~ U[band); AGE_MAX = 90; speed row = min(6, age/10 - 2)
source: Modelling decision. Round-4 U-06 verified: max sampled age across 9 A-seeds is 89, so every lookup resolves to a published Bohannon decade; 2.01 percent of residents (about 138 per run) are 80+ and receive the real 80+ row, not an extrapolation
uncertainty: The 90 ceiling is arbitrary but inert for speeds (the 80+ row applies to all of 80-89); PIT bands do not resolve ages above 65 locally
implementation: PopulationSampler age sampling + freeSpeedMean row clamp

name: pAwareInit
description: Probability a resident knows emergency shelters exist at event start
mechanism: Awareness gates the entire decision chain: unaware residents shelter in place accruing exposure until converted by outreach. Replaces the universal-awareness placeholder (A-12) with the one sourced local behavioural estimate for THIS event
source: Hines, Leickly, Petteni & Knowlton 2021, Stories from the Outside: Oregon Wildfires 2020, PSU Homelessness Research & Action Collaborative, N=73 unhoused Portland-area adults surveyed about the September 2020 event: nearly 65% did not hear about emergency shelters (aware 26/73 = 0.356)
uncertainty: 0.25-0.47 (Wilson 95% CI on 26/73); swept
implementation: ELayerSampler; GisAgent UNAWARE state; parameter pAwareInit

name: pAttemptGivenAware
description: Share of aware residents who attempted to access a shelter during the 2020 event
mechanism: Separates awareness from willingness to attempt; consumed as the E9 calibration target for the departure-hazard intercept (V38), not read directly by any code path
source: Same survey pie as V29: ACCESSED 10 of the 26 aware respondents (Hines et al. 2021, Stories from the Outside, N=73)
uncertainty: 0.2-0.6 (small n); enters only through the alphaHazard fit
implementation: E9 calibration target for alphaHazard; not read by code

name: pHeavyBelongings
description: Probability a resident has heavy belongings (cart or large possessions) raising the cost of departing for shelter
mechanism: Enters the barrier cost c_i in the departure hazard and the destination barrier penalty. Mechanism is decision latency and abandonment threshold, never a walking-speed penalty: load carriage does not slow self-selected walking (Bastien 2005, reported as a negative result in 03-MOVEMENT.md)
math: heavyBelongings ~ Bernoulli(p); p = 0.284 midpoint of the sourced bracket
source: Bracket floor: Ozarks 2024 unsheltered PIT (N=138, 10.8% cited dogs/property as the reason for skipping shelter); ceiling: CASPEH 2023 (42% had belongings confiscated within 6 months) and Herring et al. 2020 (46%, N=351); mechanism anchor: JOHS spokesperson Theriault, Street Roots 2020-09-16. Midpoint is a DECLARED ASSUMPTION (A-27)
uncertainty: full bracket 0.108-0.46 swept
implementation: ELayerSampler; GisAgent barrier cost; parameters pHeavyBelongings + barrierBelongings

name: pHasPet
description: Probability a resident has a pet
mechanism: Pets are an admission barrier where intake policy refuses animals and add a barrier cost to departure; 48.1% of owners report ever being turned away over pet policy, which caps the refusal branch. Never a speed effect
source: Henwood, Dzubur, Rhoades, St. Clair & Cox 2020, Journal of Social Distress and Homelessness 30(2): pet ownership among unsheltered adults in the LA County homeless count, 12%/9.0%/11.7% weighted over 2017-19 (n=4808/4815/4259 surveys)
uncertainty: 0.055-0.12; floor from Cronley et al. 2009 (6% of 4,100 sheltered adults, Knoxville, doi 10.2466/PR0.105.2.481-499); swept
implementation: ELayerSampler; GisAgent eligibility gate + barrier cost; parameters pHasPet + barrierPet + petPolicyDefault

name: pHasDependents
description: Probability an unsheltered adult travels with dependent children
mechanism: Dependents raise the departure barrier cost, exclude adults-only sites from the choice set, and slow the travelling group (V34). The 2020 record shows adults-only intake at the smoke shelters, so this attribute activates a real documented exclusion
source: HUD 2025 PIT Populations and Subpopulations report, CoC OR-501 (Portland/Gresham/Multnomah County): 30 unsheltered adult-plus-child households against 6,831 unsheltered adults; adults-only 2020 intake verified verbatim (Street Roots 2020-09-16: 'nearly a dozen families with children [housed] in existing shelters')
doi_or_dataset: HUD 2025 PIT OR-501 Populations and Subpopulations
uncertainty: 0.004-0.03 (0.022 = Pathways 2026 caretaker rate); swept
implementation: ELayerSampler; GisAgent eligibility gate + group speed; parameters pHasDependents + barrierDependents

name: groupSpeedDeltaMps
description: Walking-speed reduction per additional travelling group member
mechanism: Residents travelling with dependents walk at the group's pace, lengthening time outdoors and lowering the chance of reaching a bed before capacity fills. Applied as a derived per-agent field, never by mutating the sampled individual speed
math: v_group = v - delta x extraMembers with delta in [0.04 0.08] m/s
source: Moussaid, Perozo, Garnier, Helbing & Theraulaz 2010, PLoS ONE 5(4):e10047: measured pedestrian group speeds v = -0.04x+1.26 (low density) and -0.08x+1.24 (high density)
uncertainty: slope range 0.04-0.08 m/s per member swept; slowest-member rule is a labelled bounding assumption
implementation: ELayerSampler derived groupSpeedDeltaMps; GisAgent effective speed

name: sigmaTheta
description: Standard deviation of the persistent departure-propensity trait theta_i
mechanism: Trait heterogeneity staggers departures, replacing the simultaneous-departure artefact that A-02 records; theta_i also gates the Scenario-E push-through decision. sigma_T = 0 collapses to the deterministic cohort behaviour of the bright-line latch (R3 null)
math: theta_i ~ N(0, sigma_T^2), drawn unconditionally and scaled
source: No direct estimate exists for this population. Var(theta):Var(bRisk x z_R) ratio anchored 1.0-2.0 to the Kincade-fire evacuation study's persistent-trait (31%) vs momentary-cue (21%) predictor-importance split (E1 harvest record, E-LAYER-SPEC.md section 2)
uncertainty: swept 0.5-1.5; variance ratio swept 1.0-2.0
implementation: ELayerSampler theta; GisAgent hazard; parameter sigmaTheta

name: riskCue
description: Accumulated smoke risk cue z_R and its log-odds weight bRisk in the departure hazard
mechanism: Converts accumulated smoke burden into departure probability. The cue is dose-accumulating with exponential decay because the sourced behavioural response is to cumulative exposure days, not instantaneous PM2.5
math: z_R(t) decays with half-life riskHalfLifeH and accumulates f(C(t)); u_i += bRisk x z_R(t)
source: Form and direction anchored to Castillo et al., Mitigating wildfire smoke inside homes: Evidence from Oregon September 2020, Risk Analysis (online 2023, doi 10.1111/risa.14252), n=543 same-event households: number of exposure days positively associated with protective measures. Magnitude unsourced
uncertainty: bRisk swept 0.25-0.55 central and 0.2-0.8 wide; half-life swept 12-72 h
implementation: GisAgent hazard accumulator; parameters bRisk + riskHalfLifeH

name: wOfficial
description: Log-odds weight of the official shelter-activation cue in the departure hazard
mechanism: The official cue switches on at the first shelter activation tick (preserving the A-02 no-departure-before-opening gate) and raises departure odds for every aware resident
math: u_i += wOfficial x officialCue(t), officialCue = 1 from first activation
source: Anchored to the evacuation-order pooled OR 4.21 (ln = 1.44) from Tanim, Wiernik, Reader & Hu 2022, Journal of Environmental Psychology 79:101742, meta-analysis of 33 models / 29,873 households (doi 10.1016/j.jenvp.2021.101742); the mapping from mandatory-evacuation orders to voluntary shelter activation is assumed
uncertainty: swept 0.6-1.7

name: alphaHazard
description: Departure-hazard intercept
mechanism: Sets the baseline hourly departure odds for an aware barrier-free resident; fitted so the realized attempt share reproduces the E9 occupancy target (~130/198 aggregate with the ~90/40 site split) rather than asserted
math: u_i = alphaHazard + bRisk x z_R + wOfficial x cue + theta_i - c_i
source: PROVISIONAL pending the E9 calibration (A-30); initial value chosen so the implied attempt share matches pAttemptGivenAware x pAwareInit (V30 x V29 = 0.137) over the event window
uncertainty: swept +/-1 log-odds around the fitted value

name: gammaVuln
description: Susceptibility increment to the risk-cue weight for COPD / asthma / age-65+ / mobility-limited residents
mechanism: Vulnerable residents weight the same smoke cue more heavily when deciding to depart. BEHAVIOUR ONLY: susceptibility here drives departure timing and never enters dose physics (decision D-3 lineage). Asthma legitimately enters this term, so the U-19 negative control updates to: asthma may shift departure timing but never gait speed and never dose
math: bRisk_i = bRisk x (1 + gammaVuln x vulnerable_i)
source: Sign anchor: Evers et al. 2022 (n=1,200, same-event Oregon survey): vulnerable-household status POSITIVE on protective action (full citation in the E1 harvest record, E-LAYER-SPEC.md section 2; re-verify at citation time). Magnitude is an assumption
uncertainty: swept 0 to +0.5

name: barrierCostsLogOdds
description: Per-barrier log-odds costs (belongings / pet / dependents) in the departure hazard and destination utility
mechanism: Barriers suppress and delay departure and penalise barrier-hostile destinations. Hard acceptance constraint from the risk-perception-paradox literature: at maximum observed PM2.5 the high-barrier stratum must still show non-departure - a monotone risk-only trigger is forbidden
math: c_i = barrierBelongings x heavy + barrierPet x pet x petRefused + barrierDependents x dependents
source: Per-barrier anchors 0.10-0.42 log-odds from Tanim, Wiernik, Reader & Hu 2022 meta-analysis (doi 10.1016/j.jenvp.2021.101742); acceptance constraint from Wachinger, Renn, Begg & Kuhlicke 2013, The Risk Perception Paradox, Risk Analysis 33(6):1049-1065
uncertainty: each barrier cost swept 0.10-0.42 log-odds
implementation: GisAgent hazard + destination penalty; parameters barrierBelongings + barrierPet + barrierDependents

name: lambdaOutreachPerDay
description: Daily probability an unaware resident is converted to aware by outreach contact
mechanism: The only awareness-conversion channel in the Friday scope (L3 word-of-mouth is deferred, cut first under the descope ladder). No direct source exists; anchored loosely to the same survey's finding that 75% received no information during the wildfires
math: P(convert in a day) = lambdaOutreach; evaluated hourly as lambda/24
source: UNSOURCED - declared assumption (A-31), loosely anchored to Hines et al. 2021 (75% received no information during the wildfires); a real outreach-contact rate for this event does not exist in the record
uncertainty: swept 0-0.2 per day including 0 (no outreach)

name: informationRegime
description: Information regime for destination choice: 0 = L0 omniscient; 1 = L1 knows locations only
mechanism: L0 (comparator) selects among shelters with live occupancy knowledge - the full-information zero-friction upper bound that all archived runs used. L1 (new default for E arms) knows shelter LOCATIONS only and discovers fullness on arrival, matching the documented 2020 reality; discovered-full sites join a per-agent believed-full set that clears when a new site opens
math: candidate set filter at selection time
source: Infrastructure switch (like V16); the L1 semantics are grounded in the 2020 record: no live-occupancy channel existed for unhoused residents (E-LAYER-SPEC.md section 3)
uncertainty: regimes {0,1} compared explicitly; L2 (211-channel) specified but deferred
implementation: GisAgent chooseShelterByUtility vs chooseNetworkNearestShelter; parameter informationRegime

name: choiceUtilityWeights
description: Destination-choice utility weights betaT (travel time) and betaS (capacity-size prior) under L1
mechanism: V_j = -betaT x walkTime_j(ownSpeed) + betaS x ln(capacity_j) - barrierPenalty_j. The proximity-vs-admission-likelihood tradeoff the study requires emerges endogenously: fast agents discount rejection risk at near sites, slow or high-susceptibility agents prefer larger less-contested sites
math: argmax_j V_j with deterministic tie-break; logit noise deferred
source: Impedance dominance verified: Cheng, Wilmot & Baker 2008 (hurricane destination choice, DIST t = -6 in both models, supply term positive); fillRisk-as-size-prior is a DECLARED MODELLING ASSUMPTION (A-32) - no queue-avoidance estimates exist
uncertainty: betaS/betaT swept 1-2 orders of magnitude around Cheng's supply/distance marginal rate of substitution

name: shelterPolicyVariant
description: Selects whether an arm reads its archived shelter file or the _elayer variant carrying the RECORDED pet-intake policy
mechanism: 0 = the archived per-arm file byte-for-byte, which is what the R3 null must read for its identity proof to mean anything. 1 = the _elayer variant, in which pet_intake is joined from the upstream 2026 inventory's pets_allowed column (4 of 48 facilities record admit, 422 beds). The archived files are never edited, so data_version_tag and the archived three-arm chain are untouched; the variant is a separate file with its own checksum
math: shelter CSV path selection at context build; fail-fast if the variant file is absent
source: Infrastructure switch created to fix a documented-value-vs-used-value mismatch found by adversarial review: A-29 justified blanket pet refusal on the grounds the record was silent, which is true of the 2020 shelters but false of the 2026 network the E arms run. Built by scripts/build_shelter_policy_elayer.py
uncertainty: variants {0,1} compared explicitly; petPolicyDefault still swept for the genuinely unrecorded remainder
